summary: Implemented the Phase 1 manual grid surface with typed `UniformGrid`, `CustomGrid`, `CustomGridBoundaries`, and `GridSpec` models, simulation-time grid resolution, and typed grid IR lowering with resolved boundary metadata.
key_findings: `src/autofdtd/grid/specs.py` now provides concrete Phase 1 grid models plus `ResolvedGrid`/`ResolvedGridAxis` so simulations can resolve axis boundaries before compiler/runtime work lands.

`Simulation.resolved_grid()` and `core.validation` now enforce a strict top-level `GridSpec` contract, validate manual grid compatibility against simulation bounds, and reject planned-but-not-yet-implemented grid families like `AutoGrid` explicitly.

`src/autofdtd/ir/models.py` now lowers `GridSpec` into typed grid IR (`GridSpecIR`, per-axis IR, and resolved grid metadata), giving later discretization and mode-solver tasks an inspectable execution-side mesh contract.
Public exports, examples, and docs were updated so the grid surface is part of the Tidy3D-inspired API rather than an opaque dict payload.
Verification passed with `python -m ruff check src tests` and `python -m pytest` (47 tests passed).

artifacts.description: Phase 1 manual grid models, resolution helpers, and domain-to-boundary lowering.
`Simulation.resolved_grid()` integration and grid-spec validation during simulation construction.
Checklist-aware normalization for `GridSpec` and explicit rejection of not-yet-implemented grid families.
Typed grid execution IR and lowering path with resolved grid metadata.
Focused grid behavior tests covering snapping, explicit boundaries, and resolved-grid shape metrics.
Grid-scope documentation for the new Phase 1 manual discretization surface.

follow_up_notes: The next grid task can add `AutoGrid`, refinement metadata, and related planning fields onto the existing `GridSpec`/`ResolvedGrid` seam without changing simulation or IR contracts.
